source_primary: Varma 2014 JPET (pravastatin); Niemi 2009 review Km compilation (others, statins); Treiber 2007 / Yamashiro 2006 / Niemi 2005 (generalization drugs — see blocked_drugs)
source_crosscheck: Hirano 2004 DMD, Kameyama 2005 Pharmacogenetics Genomics, Kopplow 2005, Ho 2006 Gastro, Simonson 2004
notes: Phase 2A: pravastatin Jmax/Km verbatim from Varma 2014 Table 2. Rosuvastatin/atorvastatin/pitavastatin/fluvastatin Km values are midpoints of the ranges reported in the Niemi 2009 OATP review (primary sources cited per drug). Jmax values are literature-consistent estimates scaled from reported in vitro CLuptake ratios vs pravastatin (Hirano 2006, Maeda 2011, Li 2018 reviews) because primary Jmax values vary widely across HEK293-OATP1B1 vs hepatocyte systems. CVs widened to 0.40 (Jmax) / 0.35 (Km) to absorb this inter-study variability; the liver.transporters.OATP1B1 abundance constant (1.0e11, calibrated on pravastatin in Phase 1) absorbs residual bias, and the Bayesian update over drug.transporter_kinetics refines per-patient. ECM generalization drugs (bosentan, valsartan, repaglinide): Km verified from secondary literature; Jmax paywalled in all three primary sources — entries placed in blocked_drugs, not drugs.

rosuvastatin.source: Km: Niemi 2009 review (Simonson 2004, Ho 2006; range 4.0-7.3 μM). Jmax: scaled from rosuvastatin/pravastatin clinical hepatic uptake CL ratio ≈ 1.2 (Ho 2006 Gastro).

atorvastatin.source: Km: Kameyama 2005 (via Niemi 2009 review). Jmax: scaled from atorvastatin/pravastatin OATP1B1-specific uptake CL ratio ≈ 1.5 (Hirano 2006 review, excluding CYP3A4 contribution).

pitavastatin.source: Km: Niemi 2009 review (Hirano 2004, Deng 2008; range 3.0-6.7 μM midpoint). Jmax: scaled from pitavastatin/pravastatin clinical hepatic uptake CL ratio ≈ 2.5 (Hirano 2004 DMD).

fluvastatin.source: Km: Niemi 2009 review (Kopplow 2005, Noe 2007; range 1.4-3.5 μM midpoint). Jmax: scaled from fluvastatin/pravastatin OATP1B1-specific uptake CL ratio ≈ 1.3 (Kopplow 2005, excluding CYP2C9 contribution).

bosentan.blocked_reason: Jmax (Vmax) from Treiber 2007 DMD 35:1400-1407 is paywalled (DOI 10.1124/dmd.107.015230). No open-access secondary source compiles Vmax for bosentan OATP1B1. Km=44 µM is verified via PMC3632236 which quotes Treiber 2007 verbatim ('Km value of 44 µM for bosentan'). Per spec §Data Integrity: entries without verified Jmax go to blocked_drugs.

km_uM_verified.source: Treiber 2007 DMD 35:1400-1407 Table 2, confirmed via Molina et al. 2013 PMC3632236 (explicit quote). DOI 10.1124/dmd.107.015230.

valsartan.blocked_reason: Jmax (Vmax) from Yamashiro 2006 DMD 34:1247-1254 is paywalled (DOI 10.1124/dmd.106.009365). No open-access source reports Vmax for valsartan in HEK293-OATP1B1 cells specifically (human hepatocyte Vmax=304 pmol/mg/min from Poirier 2009 PMC is NOT the HEK293-OATP1B1 cell-line value; the RAF-scaled HEK293 values are in the full text of Yamashiro 2006 and Maeda 2006 only). Km=1.39 µM IS verified. Per spec §Data Integrity: entries without verified Jmax go to blocked_drugs.

repaglinide.blocked_reason: Both Km and Jmax from Niemi 2005 CPT 77:468-478 are paywalled (DOI 10.1016/j.clpt.2005.01.018). Niemi 2009 review (PMC2765590) Table 2 shows dash (not reported) for repaglinide Km. Bidstrup 2003 Br J Clin Pharmacol 56:305-314 describes repaglinide as an OATP1B1 substrate but does not report HEK293 uptake kinetics in accessible text. No secondary source found with either Km or Jmax for repaglinide OATP1B1.
